title: Amsterdam by Canal, Oost and Noord

bestPeriod.note: Tulip season runs April into early May; June and September give long light with fewer crowds than midsummer.

summary: A week of Amsterdam in rings: the UNESCO canal belt, the newer architecture of Oost and Noord, and the free ferries that cross the IJ.
hook: Amsterdam rewards a week the way a weekend never can: the canal belt stops feeling like a postcard once you have walked it three times, and the free ferries across the IJ turn Noord from an afterthought into half the trip. Book the timed-entry museums before you land, then let the neighbourhoods set the pace.

snapshot.Base(s): Jordaan or De Pijp, single base all week
snapshot.Best Period: April to June, September to October
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: 55-70 km on foot, flat, plus several short IJ ferry crossings
snapshot.Getting There: Direct train from Schiphol to Amsterdam Centraal in 15-20 min
snapshot.Who It Suits: First-time and repeat visitors who want depth over a checklist, families comfortable near bike lanes

itinerary.title: Brouwersgracht to the Golden Bend
itinerary.morning: Start at Brouwersgracht, the prettiest working canal in the belt, and walk south along Prinsengracht to the Westerkerk, Hendrick de Keyser's church of 1620-1631 with the 85 m Westertoren added in 1638. Climb the tower for the belt's clearest overview.
itinerary.afternoon: Book a timed slot at the Anne Frank House on Prinsengracht 263, inside the 1635 canal house where the Secret Annex is hidden behind the bookcase. Slots for six weeks out release online every Tuesday at 10:00 CET; a smaller batch opens two days ahead at 09:00.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in the Jordaan at Moeders on Rozengracht, a long-running Amsterdam kitchen with a wall of mismatched family photographs and honest stamppot.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km walking · districts: Grachtengordel-West, Jordaan · tickets approx €16.

itinerary.title: Jordaan and the Negen Straatjes
itinerary.morning: The Noordermarkt runs a farmers' and organic market every Saturday 09:00-16:00, and a flea and textile market every Monday 09:00-13:00; either anchors the morning. Circle the Noorderkerk (1623) before the stalls close in.
itinerary.afternoon: The Negen Straatjes, nine cross-streets between Prinsengracht and Singel, hold Amsterdam's independent shops: vintage on Berenstraat, design on Hartenstraat, specialist food on Runstraat.
itinerary.evening: A canal-side beer at Café 't Smalle on Egelantiersgracht, a former genever distillery tasting house from 1786, then dinner nearby.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km walking · districts: Jordaan, Grachtengordel-West · tickets approx €0 (market spend aside).

itinerary.title: Museumplein and the Golden Age masters
itinerary.morning: The Rijksmuseum, Pierre Cuypers' 1885 cathedral of a building, needs a booked timed slot; go straight for the Gallery of Honour and Rembrandt's Night Watch before the tour groups arrive at 10:30.
itinerary.afternoon: The Van Gogh Museum next door, Gerrit Rietveld's 1973 building plus Kisho Kurokawa's 1999 exhibition wing, releases tickets ten weeks ahead on Mondays at 10:00 and sells out for weekends within days.
itinerary.evening: Walk into Vondelpark for the open-air light, then dinner in Oud-Zuid on Cornelis Schuytstraat.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km walking · districts: Museumkwartier, Oud-Zuid · tickets approx €47.

itinerary.title: Oost
itinerary.morning: The Dappermarkt runs Monday to Saturday, 09:00-17:00, one of the city's most genuinely local street markets, Surinamese, Turkish and Dutch stalls side by side. This is the week's food anchor.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Muiderpoort, the 1770 city gate Napoleon rode through in 1811, then into the Amstelkwartier, where recent housing blocks by young Dutch practices face the Amstel across the water. The Tropenmuseum (Cuypers en Hulswit, 1926) covers a wet-weather hour well.
itinerary.evening: Dinner on Javastraat, Oost's food street, or Balistraat nearby.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km walking · districts: Oost, Dapperbuurt, Amstelkwartier · tickets approx €17.

itinerary.title: Noord across the IJ
itinerary.morning: Take the free GVB ferry from behind Centraal Station to Buiksloterweg, it runs every few minutes, day and night, and carries pedestrians, cyclists and prams at no charge. EYE Filmmuseum, Delugan Meissl's angular white building from 2012, sits right at the landing.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk or cycle along the NDSM-weg to NDSM-werf, a former shipyard now covered in murals, with the STRAAT street-art museum inside an old warehouse and the Kunststad studio complex.
itinerary.evening: Ride up A'DAM Lookout for the sunset view back over the Centraal Station roofline, then the free ferry home.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km walking, 25 min on ferries · districts: Noord (Buiksloterham, NDSM) · tickets approx €15.

itinerary.title: De Pijp and Amsterdam School Zuid
itinerary.morning: The Albert Cuypmarkt, Monday to Saturday 09:00-17:00, runs the length of Albert Cuypstraat and is the country's largest daily street market, herring, stroopwafels, fabric and flowers in one 500 m stretch.
itinerary.afternoon: Sarphatipark for a break, then south into the Rivierenbuurt for De Dageraad, the 1918-1923 housing block by Michel de Klerk and Piet Kramer near Burgemeester Tellegenstraat, Amsterdam School brick expressionism at its most sculptural.
itinerary.evening: Dinner in De Pijp, still Amsterdam's densest restaurant neighbourhood per block.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km walking · districts: De Pijp, Rivierenbuurt · tickets approx €5.

itinerary.title: Nieuwmarkt, Plantage and Waterlooplein
itinerary.morning: Nieuwmarkt square and the Waag, a 1488 city-gate turned weigh house, then north up Zeedijk through the old sailors' quarter into Chinatown.
itinerary.afternoon: The Plantage: Hortus Botanicus (one of the world's oldest botanical gardens, founded 1638), and the Portuguese Synagogue (Elias Bouman, 1675), centrepiece of the Jewish Cultural Quarter.
itinerary.evening: Browse the Waterlooplein flea market before it closes at 18:00, then a last canal-side dinner near the Amstel, book a self-drive electric sloop from one of the canal-belt rental docks for a final hour on the water if the weather holds.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km walking · districts: Nieuwmarkt, Plantage, Waterlooplein · tickets approx €12.

accommodationStrategy.name: The Toren
accommodationStrategy.description: A pair of connected 17th-century canal houses on the Keizersgracht, close enough to the Jordaan and the Anne Frank House to make Days 1 and 2 entirely on foot. Rooms are small, as every canal house is, ask for one facing the water, not the courtyard.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 8-10 weeks ahead for spring and September.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Not Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: A converted school on Piri Reisplein with rooms built as a houseboat, a caravan and a tram carriage among conventional ones. It sits between the Jordaan and Museumplein, a genuine ten-minute walk to either, and works well for families who want a talking point as much as a bed.

accommodationStrategy.name: Sir Adam
accommodationStrategy.location: base of the A'DAM Tower, Noord
accommodationStrategy.description: Puts Day 5 on your doorstep and turns the ferry commute into the fun part of the evening rather than the end of it. The rooftop bar looks straight down the IJ to Centraal Station.

logistics.emergency: 112 for police, fire and ambulance; canal water rescue is handled by the same number.

other.label: GVB fares
other.text: Contactless bank cards and phones tap in and out on buses, trams, the metro and the HADAG-style IJ ferries via OVpay, charged per journey capped daily. Multi-day GVB passes (24 through 168 hours) are better value if you are moving constantly; buy them in the GVB app or at Centraal Station.

other.label: The IJ ferries to Noord are free
other.text: for pedestrians and cyclists on the Buiksloterweg, IJplein and NDSM routes, no ticket, no tap, just walk on.

other.label: Timed-entry windows
other.text: Anne Frank House: six weeks out, Tuesdays 10:00 CET, plus a same-week release two days ahead at 09:00. Van Gogh Museum: ten weeks out, Mondays 10:00. Rijksmuseum: slots open roughly three months ahead and rarely sell out except peak weekends.

other.label: Bike lanes are traffic
other.text: The red-asphalt paths beside every canal carry real cyclist speed; look both ways before stepping onto one, always.

other.label: Cash is nearly extinct
other.text: Contactless card or phone covers almost everything, including most markets now; carry some coins only for the rare stall that does not.

other.label: Tourist tax
other.text: Amsterdam charges a per-night city tax on top of the room rate, usually already included in the quoted price, check at booking.

other.label: Opening-hour trap
other.text: Many independent shops in the Negen Straatjes open at 11:00 or later and close Sundays or Mondays; the Albert Cuyp and Dappermarkt run Monday-Saturday only.

other.label: Emergencies
other.text: 112 for police, fire and ambulance; canal water rescue is handled by the same number.

proTips: Buy Anne Frank House and Van Gogh Museum tickets the moment you fix your dates, both routinely sell out weeks ahead in the April-June and September windows.
Take the NDSM ferry (not the Buiksloterweg one) in the late afternoon on Day 5; it runs a longer, quieter crossing and times well with sunset at the Lookout.
Walk the Rijksmuseum's Gallery of Honour first, before the museum's own opening rush from tour buses arrives around 10:30.
The Noordermarkt's Saturday farmers' stalls thin out fast after 13:00, go early for the good cheese.
Skip the fixed-route canal cruises: a GVB day ticket covering the IJ ferries plus a short Amstel stretch on tram 4 shows you more water for less money.
De Pijp empties of tourists after 21:00 even in July; it is the neighbourhood to walk for an unhurried evening.

packingNotes: A proper rain shell, Amsterdam weather turns inside twenty minutes most of the year.
Flat, grippy shoes for cobbles and canal-house thresholds that are rarely level.
A cross-body bag rather than a backpack on trams and in markets.
A phone or card that supports contactless tap-in for OVpay; a physical OV-chipkaart is now mostly a backup.
A tote for the Albert Cuyp and Dappermarkt; stalls sell by weight and hand you paper, not bags.
Sunglasses and a hat for the Vondelpark and Sarphatipark stretches in late spring.
A light scarf or layer for the open ferry decks even in summer, the IJ has real wind.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Anne Frank House or Van Gogh Museum sells out your date.** Check the official sites for daily cancellation releases at 09:00, or shift the visit to a weekday morning slot if one remains.
**Rain wipes out a walking afternoon.** The Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum, Tropenmuseum and EYE Filmmuseum all absorb two to three hours indoors without rebooking anything.
**A ferry line is suspended for maintenance or fog.** The Metro 52 Noord/Zuidlijn runs Centraal Station to Noorderpark on the same fare system as a backup route into Noord.
**You misjudge a bike lane.** Cross at marked points, look for the painted bike symbol, and never walk in the red asphalt strip even to take a photo.
**A market day falls on your planned rest day.** The Dappermarkt and Albert Cuyp run Monday-Saturday; only build market mornings into weekdays, not a Sunday.
